summary: Klamath NF lookout near Orleans: first station possibly 1919, enclosed tower built 1933, gone by 1986; the 2020 site has only a rock monument.

facts.design: USFS R1 Plan cabin on an 18-foot enclosed timber tower (1933 structure)
facts.status_note: Gone by 1986 per the Thornton Survey; a 2020 bike guide describes only a rock monument at the site.

staffing.status: last reported keeper 1971; no later staffing found

facts.agency: US Forest Service - Klamath National Forest

visit.trail_note: A 2020 bike route guide describes an optional steep climb, 1.5 miles each way, to the old site from a loop that starts in Somes Bar.

events.note: FFLOS says the original structure may have been constructed as early as 1919

New cabin on an 18-foot enclosed timber tower about 100 yards from the old site; finished in late 1933
Road to Offield Lookout and Camp 3 completed
Aircraft Warning Service used the station as an observation post during the winter months
Wilford Ferris and wife replaced Prigmore as lookout
Ida Lake went on the lookout for the Ukonom District, April 1966
Ida Lake serving as lookout (Ukonom District) in 1971
Structure still standing in 1981 per FFLOS
Gone by 1986 (Thornton Survey); FFLOS says removed prior to 1986, so this year is an upper bound
2020 bike guide describes only a rock monument at the site
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register April 22, 2020

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS says the original lookout may date to 1919 and the enclosed tower was completed in 1933. The Siskiyou Daily News reported a new station completed in October 1921. The sources do not say whether the 1921 station and FFLOS's original structure are the same.

notes_for_editor: Today's status rests on one 2020 bike route guide, not a survey or site visit. Access level is omitted: no source states whether the site is open to visitors, and the 1971 access note is historical. The 1919 date is hedged in FFLOS ('may have been'). The 1921 station may or may not be the same structure as FFLOS's original; the brief's 1933 build date is correct for the enclosed tower. No photos added: captions only (a 1981 photo credited to the Siskiyou County Historical Society via FFLOS; 1981 and 2009 photo credits on the Siskiyou County page), and no image URLs were retrieved. The 1971 'Ida Lake' staffing is the last keeper found; later staffing is unknown.
